flow.d: Resin, pigment, pails, lids and labels are kept with all the other stock, in locations set by part number rather than by how close they are to the lines.
Each line holds one load of each material: one pallet of pails, one drum of resin.
An operator calls a material handler when a load runs out. The line stops until the next load arrives from the store.
Every refill is a round trip of about 60 to 100 m between the store and the line.
A few loads of each line material are kept in racks next to the lines, refilled from the store by forklift.
Still one load of each material at the line, still called when it runs out.
A refill is a few metres from the supermarket, so the line stops for less time each run-out.
When a supermarket face is down to two loads, the forklift brings more from the store, between inbound put-aways.
The same supermarket, refilled from the store by forklift.
Each material has two loads at the line. When the first runs out, the line runs on the second and a kanban card goes up.
A handler collects the cards and delivers every carded load in one loop, on a fixed timetable.
Two bins instead of one means more stock and more floor space at the lines, in return for fewer stops.

steps.t: Central store, no issue booking, line materials in the store faces nearest the lines
Line-side supermarket, called when a load runs out
Central store, two bins at the line, called when the first runs out
Supermarket, two bins at the line, called when the first runs out
Supermarket, two bins and a 20-minute milk run
